subject: Urgent: Production timeouts and 5xx/429 burst - Dedicated pool impact
messages:
From: Lucas Ortega <lucas@northbridge-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@northbridge-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike — urgent

Hi Kimberly,

We just started seeing a large burst of 5xx and 429 responses from your API for our dedicated pool (customer pool id NB-POOL-07). The issue began ~08:50 PT and is causing timeouts in our ingestion pipeline — several downstream jobs have failed retries and backlog is growing.

Attached is a short log snippet and a screenshot from our monitoring. Key details:
- ~30% error rate on calls to the generation route between 08:50–09:05
- majority are 5xx (504/500) and some 429s; client retry amplification observed
- latency for successful calls jumped from 120ms median to ~1.2s

This is production impacting. Can you confirm receipt and let us know immediate mitigation steps and ETA for a fix? We will need an incident summary and any credit guidance.

Thanks,
Lucas
Head of Platform — NorthBridge Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike — urgent

Quick triage:
- Autoscaler for NB-POOL-07 experienced repeated allocation timeouts to new worker nodes between 08:42–08:58. The control plane queued scale requests but the infra backplane returned transient failures (quota-like allocation 429s from the provider).
- As a result, the request queue grew and our serving runtime began returning 504s under heavy concurrency; retry amplification made the spike worse.

Short-term mitigation applied (09:20):
- Manually started 4 standby instances into NB-POOL-07 (should add ~18 inference workers).
- Engaged fallback routing: new requests for non-critical routes are routed to a lower-memory model variant to reduce per-request GPU memory churn.

ETA: the manual workers are coming up now — expect error rate to drop in 10–15m. Follow-ups: we need to loosen the autoscaler retry window and add an emergency bypass path for provider allocation failures.

Action items for post-mortem:
- Add provider allocation failure detection metric and alert
- Add early tail-shed policy to avoid retry amplification (client-facing guidance + server-side short-circuit)

—Rishi (oncall lead)

Markus — quick executive summary and ask for approval to proceed with a proactive goodwill credit:

Incident summary:
- Impact window: 2027-04-19 08:50 PT — 2027-04-19 09:35 PT (error spike and elevated tail latency for NB-POOL-07).
- Root cause (initial): provider allocation timeouts caused autoscaler failures -> queue growth -> serving runtime returning 5xx under load; retry amplification worsened impact.
- Mitigation: manual capacity added at 09:20 PT, route-level fallbacks enabled and removed at 09:35 PT; system stable thereafter.

Customer impact: ingestion jobs delayed; ~45 minutes of elevated error rates/latency affecting their nightly pipeline. Customer requested credit guidance.

Proposed remedy:
- One-week pro-rated service credit for NB-POOL-07 equivalent to 20% of one-week planned usage (goodwill).
- Operational follow-ups: autoscaler tuning, provider allocation failure alerting, and a post-mortem shared with the customer within 48 hours.

Please approve or propose adjustments. I’ll coordinate communication and finalize the post-incident note to share with NorthBridge.

—Kimberly Park
